findings.text: `eval "printf -v test_description '%s' \"$2\""` executes the description text as shell code. A test named like `@test "foo $(rm -rf x)"` or one containing a double quote or backtick runs commands, or breaks with a syntax error, when the test is registered.

`[[ ${BATS_TEST_NAME-} == $* ]]` leaves `$*` unquoted, so it is treated as a glob pattern. Test function names containing `*`, `?` or `[` can match the wrong test and set tags and command for a different test. Quote it as `"$*"`.

`bats_test_begin` was removed, but callers such as bats-exec-test and the preprocessor may still invoke it. That would fail with command not found, and the `begin` extended-syntax output and the `setup` call would be lost. Also, `bats_test_function` now exits 1 on any unrecognized first argument, which breaks old-style calls like `bats_test_function test_name`.
